specializations.name: Character Design & Identity
specializations.inputs: Approved styleframes, role, silhouette, personality cues, expression examples and allowed viewpoints
specializations.decision: Define a canonical model sheet, shape language, proportion ratios, palette, recognizable markers and permitted variation for a character.
specializations.mechanism: A stable character identity sheet with explicit invariants can reduce visual drift across shots and control changes.
specializations.tradeoff: A single flattering reference hides viewpoint and occlusion uncertainty; excessive constraints can suppress expressive poses.
specializations.verification: Compare the neutral design and at least three acting poses at intended crops, viewpoints and lighting; check landmarks, silhouette and recognizability.
specializations.output: Character identity sheet, proportions, landmarks, permissible expression and pose range
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Character Anatomy & Construction
specializations.inputs: Character identity sheet, required action set, pose extremes, visible views and procedural boundary
specializations.decision: Specify articulation and deformation regions for stylized or realistic bodies and choose cutout, vector path, layered 2.5D or procedural 3D construction.
specializations.mechanism: Pose-aware segment and deformation plans can keep the visible form coherent at the required angles.
specializations.tradeoff: Overly literal anatomical joints may limit stylization; a still photo cannot establish unseen body structure.
specializations.verification: Render turnarounds or planned views and stress silhouette, limb proportions, topology and deformation at action extremes.
specializations.output: Procedural anatomy map, controllable segments, joints and deformation envelope
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Character Asset System
specializations.inputs: Canonical character design, construction plan, scene requirements and versioned source parameters
specializations.decision: Create a reusable parameterized master character with stable object/part IDs and project-specific variants separated from animation.
specializations.mechanism: One source of character geometry and identity may prevent shot-by-shot redrawing and enable predictable revisions.
specializations.tradeoff: Rigid sharing can break camera-specific corrective shapes; imported rigs require declared provenance and may violate a code-only boundary.
specializations.verification: Instantiate the same master asset in two dissimilar scenes, vary pose and view, then compare identity and verify stable handles.
specializations.output: Versioned reusable character definition, expression targets, part IDs and approved overrides
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Advanced Rigging & Skinning
specializations.inputs: Character anatomy, rest pose, controllable parts, joint motion limits and intended shots
specializations.decision: Construct 2D parenting/deformation controls or 3D bones, inverse kinematics, skin weights and corrective shapes as needed; define solve order.
specializations.mechanism: A controllable rig can coordinate multiple parts during body and facial animation without redrawing each frame.
specializations.tradeoff: Joint flips, unstable IK, volume loss and skin collapse can emerge at extreme poses, especially with cyclic constraints.
specializations.verification: Test reachable targets, joint limits, blend shapes, extreme bends, reverse seeking and reproducible deformations.
specializations.output: Evaluable rig, pose interface, weight maps or deformation rules, solver constraints
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Body Mechanics & Locomotion
specializations.inputs: Rig, mass/scale convention, action goals, path, environment contacts and rhythm
specializations.decision: Author balanced poses, weight transfer, gait cycles, contact timing, anticipation, follow-through and physical or stylized arcs.
specializations.mechanism: Controlled contact and timing can make locomotion readable and convey mass, intent and momentum.
specializations.tradeoff: Foot sliding, unstable balance, penetrations or over-mechanical cycles can make behavior implausible; stylistic exaggeration may be deliberate.
specializations.verification: Inspect feet/contact trajectories, planted phases, center-of-mass estimates, cycle seam and full-speed playback over repeated steps.
specializations.output: Reusable contact-aware body action with pose keyframes and cycle parameters
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Facial Animation & Expressions
specializations.inputs: Facial construction, rig, emotional beats, eye target, design constraints and camera crop
specializations.decision: Design expression shapes, brows, gaze, eyelids, cheek/mouth deformation, pose combinations and timing with an expressive but stable face.
specializations.mechanism: Coordinated gaze and facial deformation can communicate attention and emotion while retaining character identity.
specializations.tradeoff: Expression controls may conflict, clip through surfaces or lose readability at small scales; emotion cannot be proved from expression alone.
specializations.verification: Check neutral and emotion transitions, left/right asymmetry, blink extremes, mouth-eye coordination and full-shot viewing size.
specializations.output: Expression library, facial rig channels, emotional pose and gaze tracks
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Dialogue & Lip Synchronization
specializations.inputs: Approved dialogue, actually rendered or recorded speech, verified timing or phoneme alignment, viseme library and facial rig
specializations.decision: Map timed phonemes or reviewed acoustic cues to mouth poses, coarticulation and holds; preserve acting expressions and dialogue performance.
specializations.mechanism: Audio-timed visemes plus transition shaping can align recognizable mouth movement to spoken speech.
specializations.tradeoff: Text-only timings and raw audio duration do not establish phoneme timing; visemes can clash with emotion or oversaturate the mouth.
specializations.verification: Listen and watch encoded dialogue at normal speed; check hard consonants, open vowels, offsets, pauses, mouth closure and desynchronization over long shots.
specializations.output: Audio-bound viseme track, timing provenance and tested lip-sync shot
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Character Acting & Performance
specializations.inputs: Character role, scene objectives, storyboard beats, dialogue/emotion and shot/framing
specializations.decision: Translate intent into anticipations, pose accents, gaze changes, gesture phrases, holds and action transitions; orchestrate body and facial tracks.
specializations.mechanism: Contrast between meaningful poses and controlled timing can make a character action intelligible and motivated.
specializations.tradeoff: Generic gestures, excessive motion, competing gestures and mismatch with spoken intent reduce clarity.
specializations.verification: Review blocking with sound off, then full performance with sound; test poses and silhouette, emotional transition and acting continuity.
specializations.output: Shot-based performance plan and synchronized body/face/gaze action tracks
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Multi-Character Interaction & Contact
specializations.inputs: Two or more character rigs, shared scene coordinates, props, communication beats and blocking
specializations.decision: Coordinate eyelines, turn-taking, distance, occlusion, contact targets, prop handoffs and collision or stylized overlap rules.
specializations.mechanism: Explicit shared constraints and interaction beats can improve spatial and social coherence between actors.
specializations.tradeoff: Competing rig constraints, contact jitter, impossible reach, blocking ambiguity and timing collisions arise in multi-actor scenes.
specializations.verification: Inspect interaction at entrance, touch and exit; test both camera and spatial views, occlusion, eye contact and prop ownership changes.
specializations.output: Scene-level interaction constraints, actor tracks, handoff ownership and collision checks
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.

specializations.name: Character Continuity & Performance Evaluation
specializations.inputs: Master character, approved styleframes, shots, rigs, animation tracks and final encoded footage
specializations.decision: Audit recurring visual identity, acting logic, rig stability, phoneme/audio synchronization, model reuse and cross-shot geography.
specializations.mechanism: Independent repeated checks across shot boundaries can catch character-specific errors missed by generic motion inspection.
specializations.tradeoff: Passing still-frame tests cannot prove convincing performance; successful playback cannot prove source asset provenance.
specializations.verification: Compare character landmarks across all shots, inspect cut frames and stress poses, play encoded clips at target speed, verify audio offset when dialogue exists.
specializations.output: Character acceptance record and targeted correction list tied to the responsible owners
specializations.evidence: Operational animation hypothesis; confirm with actual project playback and frame/pose inspection.
